fix: In 'Petals ... divided nearly to the base, the 10 lobes ..., L long, W wide', the sizes belong to the lobes named just before them, not to the petal. By the earlier rule, petal lobe = corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006).
reason: The width 0.5–1.2 mm is given for the 10 petal lobes, not for whole petals.
Needles (leaves) are straight or curved. The alternatives are recorded correctly.

fix: In 'X to Y at the base', 'at the base' must move the quality onto the base of the blade, as 'apex X' already does. The place phrase that comes after the values was missed.
reason: Rounded to cordate is said of the blade base. The whole blade is ovate or oblong-obovate.

fix: In orchid lip descriptions ('lip ...; lateral lobes ...; mid-lobe ...'), 'lateral lobes' are lip lobes, not leaf blade lobes. Take the organ from the lip named just before.
reason: In Vanda, the subfalcate lateral lobes belong to the lip (labellum), not to a leaf.
Erect-spreading leaves = semi erect, as the review rule says.
The silicle is notched at the tip. Emarginate already means an apex notch, so putting it on the fruit is fine.
A pedicel that lengthens and thickens in fruit is accrescent, and the fruiting stage is recorded.

fix: In 'apex X or Y', 'apex' should move the quality onto the apex part, as it does for single values (compare A00021). Here the place word was lost when the phrase had alternatives.
reason: Acute or obtuse is said of the leaf apex, not of the whole blade (which is described separately).

fix: In French floras, 'Fleurs ♀' / 'Fleurs ♂' start a section about one sex. That sex must be kept for every statement in the section.
reason: Only the female flowers are said to be subsessile or pedicellate. Male flowers are described separately.
In 'Herbs ... H × W dm' the second number is the width. 1–2.5 dm = 10–25 cm.

fix: When the outer part has no matching upper-side class in PO, keep the outer part (leaflet) with 'adaxial' as a place slot. Do not swap in the upper side of the whole leaf.
reason: The flora says the leaflets are glabrous above. The annotation moved this to the upper surface of the whole leaf.
Panicles ± puberulous: inflorescence puberulous, marked approximate.
1–4 blade lobes on each side, with the 'each side' position recorded.
(5–)7–13 dm = 70–130 cm, with a lower extreme of 50 cm. The inflorescence rises from the rosette, so height is acceptable.
Yellow-whitish = a yellowish white. White marked approximate is acceptable.

fix: For 'N-seeded' after a fruit or pod description, the rule (seeded → seed) must record the fruit as the whole being counted. Without it the number reads as seeds per plant.
reason: The flora gives 8–12 seeds per pod, not 8–12 seeds in total.
The fruiting bracteole surface ranges from densely tuberculate to smooth.
Perianth puberulous when young, with young (PATO_0000309) in the context.
Plants 4–7.5 dm tall = 40–75 cm. (The upper extreme of 10 dm is not recorded, but that does not make it false.)
The lower blade surface is hairy. The hair colour is just not recorded.

fix: The part named in the clause ('filaments ..., equal to sepals') is the part being compared. It must not be widened to stamen.
reason: The filaments are as long as the sepals, not the whole stamens.
Petal apex emarginate.
Fruit brown.
Stems up to 60 cm. Since the stems are ascending, length would be a better quality than height, but the statement is not false.

fix: 'Inner tepals' should map to tepal, not sepal. And in 'apex X or Y', 'apex' should move the quality onto the apex.
reason: Rumex has tepals, and obtuse or subacute is said of the apex of the inner tepals.

fix: 'Staminate flowers:' / 'Pistillate flowers:' headings must set the sex for every statement under them.
reason: Two petals are given only for the staminate flowers. Pistillate flowers are described separately.
Étamines nombreuses = many stamens, recorded as present with count word 'many'.
Seeds ± pitted = foveate, marked approximate.

fix: For corolla 'lobes ... glabrous inside', keep corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006) with the inner side as a place slot. Do not swap in petal adaxial epidermis.
reason: In this fused corolla, only the lobes are glabrous inside. The tube has a ring of hairs inside, so 'petal glabrous inside' is too broad.

target: floral (labellum) spur – no class found; candidate for a new FLOPO anatomy class
fix: In flower and lip descriptions, 'spur' means a nectar spur, not a short shoot (spur shoot). A shoot reading should only be used for 'spur shoots' / 'short shoots' on stems.
reason: This spur hangs from the orchid lip and is curved forward. It is not a short shoot.
